citation: Markus Nielbock and Marco J. Türk. (2017). The Engine of Life. AstroEDU manuscript no. astroedu1624. https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09766
title: First-order luminosity-scaling formula for the circumstellar habitable-zone distance
description: The article derives a first-order expression for where an Earth-like planet would orbit a star: the habitable-zone distance in AU equals the square root of the stellar luminosity in solar luminosities, because "Of ﬁrst order, this distance scales with the luminosity of the star." Activity 2 uses it to estimate the habitable-zone distance of Kepler-62 before students compare it with a sophisticated model calculation.
requirements: The luminosity of the target star relative to the solar luminosity, as tabulated for Kepler-62 in the activity.
constraints: First-order approximation only: the article notes the habitable zone is not a well-defined range and depends on many properties that allow water to be present in liquid form, and the formula neglects the stellar surface temperature.
target_learners: Students aged 12-16 in middle and secondary school
target_learning_goals: Understanding that the size and extent of a habitable zone depends on the luminosity of a star
key_sources: Markus Nielbock and Marco J. Türk. (2017). The Engine of Life. AstroEDU manuscript no. astroedu1624. https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09766
